question: Which operations learn quantities or make data-dependent decisions and must therefore not use the final test participants? Select all correct answers.

options.text: Calculating the mean and standard deviation for scaling
options.feedback: Scaling parameters are learned from whichever rows they are fit on.

options.text: Choosing features based on their correlation with the target
options.feedback: This directly uses the target values of every row it is computed from.
The component directions are learned from whichever rows they are fit on.

options.text: Calculating median values for filling missing data
options.feedback: The fill value is a quantity learned from whichever rows it is computed from.

options.text: Selecting a model parameter from performance results
options.feedback: This uses the outcome on whichever rows produced those performance results.
Model fitting learns directly from whichever rows are passed to it.

options.text: Choosing in advance whether success will be summarized with F1, ROC-AUC, or another metric
options.feedback: A metric choice made in advance, from the scientific question, does not learn anything from participant data.

successFeedback: The first six operations learn quantities or make decisions from observed data. They may use training data—and validation data where appropriate—but they must not use the final test participants. A performance metric should be chosen in advance from the scientific question and the costs of different errors; it is not learned from the participant data.
nuance: Choosing a metric only after inspecting which one makes a model look best is still poor research practice, but it is different from fitting preprocessing or a model on the test participants.
